summary: F3: Ten sign-ins originate from Portugal via university VPN vpn-edge-02 on device LT-3104, consistent with expected remote access. All four analyst claims—impossible travel, anomalous ASN, password spray, and KEV-listed VPN appliance—were rejected by the Critic with documented explanations. No compromise signal remains. Verdict: benign (confidence 0.85).

findings.claim: Most sign-ins come from PT (10 events)

rejected_claims.claim: Impossible travel: Manisa → Lisbon in 32 min
rejected_claims.reason: critic: premature impossible-travel claim: the TR event is a non-interactive mail-sync token (ExchangeSync/15), not the person; the PT sign-ins use university VPN vpn-edge-02 from device LT-3104

rejected_claims.claim: Suspicious sign-ins from an ASN outside the account's baseline: Turkcell (TR), 1 event(s)
rejected_claims.reason: critic: shared-egress ASN: 201 distinct accounts completed MFA from 193.140.10.21 in the last 30 days (threshold 10); this ASN is the organisation's own exit (shared NAT / mail relay), not a new personal network for the user

rejected_claims.claim: Password spray then success: 193.140.10.21 failed against 54 accounts (60 failures) and later signed in as this user
rejected_claims.reason: critic: 193.140.10.21 looks like shared egress: 201 distinct accounts completed MFA from this IP in the last 30 days (threshold 10); failures across many accounts are expected background noise, not a coordinated spray

rejected_claims.claim: VPN appliance vpn-edge-02 (firmware 22.7R2.8) runs a product listed in CISA KEV (CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282, …)
rejected_claims.reason: critic: firmware 22.7R2.8 already includes the fixes for the KEV entries we can version-check (CVE-2025-22457, CVE-2025-0282)

actions.action: Confirm device LT-3104 ownership and MFA enrollment for prof.kaya@aegean.edu to validate legitimate account use.
Baseline shared egress IP 193.140.10.21 against organizational NAT/mail-relay patterns to suppress false anomalies.
Validate vpn-edge-02 firmware 22.7R2.8 patch status against CISA KEV CVEs and schedule routine verification.
Maintain standard authentication monitoring; no containment or credential reset is indicated at this time.

limitations:
Authentication logs only; endpoint and mailbox telemetry were not reviewed.
Confidence bounded by single-source sign-in data and Critic-rejected contextual claims.
not_checked:

ExchangeSync/15 token activity not correlated beyond TR event attribution.

risk.rationale: All suspicious signals for prof.kaya@aegean.edu were investigated and rejected with valid critics: the TR event is a non-interactive mail-sync token (ExchangeSync/15), not a person; the Portugal sign-ins use the university VPN vpn-edge-02 from known device LT-3104; the Turkcell/shared-egress IP 193.140.10.21 is the org's own exit with 201 distinct accounts completing MFA in 30 days (far above the 10 threshold), so cross-account failures are background noise not a spray; and the VPN appliance firmware 22.7R2.8 already includes the cited CISA KEV fixes. The only verified finding is F3 [LIKELY 0.5] (most sign-ins from PT, 10 events), which is consistent with legitimate VPN use from device LT-3104 and does not indicate compromise. No data-quality conflicts. Suspicious signals are explained away.
